---
title: "Image quilting"
subtitle: "Patchwork from the book"
---

## In plain words

Instead of single stitches, the computer cuts small square pieces out of the book and lays them down like a patchwork, row by row, each piece slightly overlapping the ones already placed. It chooses pieces whose overlapping edge agrees with what is already there.

Where two pieces overlap it cuts along the wiggly line where they disagree least, so the seams are hard to see. The method is from Efros and Freeman (2001).

## The setting

**Block size.** Small blocks are mixed more freely and give a busier, more invented texture. Large blocks bring whole chunks of the book along, which looks very authentic but copies more: watch the ochre grow as the blocks get bigger.

## Good at, weak at

| Good at | Weak at |
|---|---|
| Fast and very book-like | With large blocks it is mostly reassembling the book |
| Keeps larger shapes intact | |
